title: Wire follow-up Outcomes into Dataset Candidate creation
purpose: Add only the accepted follow-up Outcome source candidate to the existing record_outcome transaction, independently from the separate evidence-association integration.
success_outcome: A newly committed Outcome atomically creates one follow_up_outcome Dataset Candidate with exactly its typed Outcome ref, follow_up_seen=true, default false trainability, and creation event; Outcome/candidate/audit failures roll back the Task completion and Outcome together, exact request retry returns the existing graph without duplicate, and FT-012 responses/authority remain unchanged.
anti_goals: Enriching other candidates from Outcome evidence refs, changing Outcome request/response/evidence grammar, lifecycle transitions, curator runtime, or historical backfill.
evidence_required: FT-014-AC-011 RED: after TASK-047 and before this wiring, a created Outcome has no source-identity candidate; GREEN: one exact raw/default follow_up_outcome candidate and event commit in the same UoW; decisive comparison: created versus exact duplicate versus conflicting request, rollback in both directions, archive/revoke race and unchanged RecordOutcomeResultV1; artifact: focused PostgreSQL transcript under .tasks/TASK-053-T3-FT-014-W2/.
constraints: Task & Follow-Up owns record_outcome UoW and passes only the new persisted Outcome identity to the Dataset creation seam.
Exact duplicate recovery returns the existing Outcome/candidate graph and performs no new Timeline append; conflicting request remains conflict.
invariants: Outcome evidence remains audit/later-review context and does not promote Plant state or Dataset trainability directly.
Archive/revoke/current ActorContext guards stay authoritative at the Outcome write boundary.
verification_targets: FT-014-AC-011: created/duplicate/conflict/no_data/evidenced/archive/revoke/audit-failure/DB-failure matrix with exact Task, Outcome, candidate and event rows plus unchanged public result.
